title: Wheel Alignment After Winter: Why Spring Is the Right Time in Calgary

Wheel Alignment After Winter: Why Spring Is the Right Time in Calgary

Calgary winters are hard on your wheels. Between freeze-thaw cycles, pothole season on the Deerfoot, and that curb you clipped in February during a snowstorm, your wheel alignment takes a beating. Spring is the right time to get it checked — and your seasonal tire changeover is the natural moment to catch problems before they cost you a set of tires.

The short version

  • Calgary's pothole season (roughly February through April) is the biggest alignment threat of the year
  • Signs of alignment problems: pulling to one side, a crooked steering wheel, or uneven edge wear on your outgoing tires
  • Spring is the best window: catch winter damage before summer kilometres wear down fresh tires unevenly
  • Prince Tires handles the tire side — seasonal swap, mount, balance, TPMS, rotation — and can flag wear patterns that suggest an alignment problem
  • Alignment itself requires a licensed auto shop with an alignment rack; book that immediately after your changeover
  • Catching issues early protects your new tires from day one

What Calgary winters do to your wheels

Your wheel alignment is set to precise angles — camber, toe, and caster — that keep your tires pointing straight and wearing evenly. Winter chips away at those angles in a few different ways.

Potholes are the main event. Calgary's pothole season typically peaks from mid-February through April as the freeze-thaw cycle breaks up pavement. Even a moderate impact at 50 km/h can shift a tie rod or knock a control arm enough to push your alignment noticeably out of spec. Drive the right stretch of Macleod Trail or Crowchild in March and you'll hit a dozen candidates in one commute.

Frost heaves and uneven pavement work more slowly but add up. Small repeated bumps accumulate over a season. By the time the roads dry out, your steering wheel might sit two or three degrees off-centre — subtle enough to chalk up to road crown, real enough that your front tires are wearing faster on one edge.

Add in the occasional snow bank, a hidden curb under slush, or a parking lot impact in the dark, and most Calgary cars come out of winter with alignment that is at least worth checking.

Signs your alignment is off

You do not need a gauge to spot a problem. These are the most common tells:

  • Pulling left or right. On a straight, flat road with no crown, let go of the wheel briefly. A well-aligned car tracks straight with no input.
  • A crooked steering wheel. If the wheel is not centred when you are driving straight, your alignment is almost certainly off.
  • Uneven tire wear. When you bring your car in for a spring changeover at Prince Tires, the tires coming off can tell the full story. Edge wear concentrated on one side of the tread is a reliable sign.
  • Vibration at highway speeds. This can also indicate a balancing issue — which tire balancing addresses — but if a fresh balance does not fix it, alignment is the next place to look.

If you are noticing a combination of these — say, a slight pull and a steering wheel that sits five degrees right at 100 km/h — do not wait until fall. That is already wearing your tires unevenly every day.

Why spring is the right time to deal with it

The practical answer: your car is already on a lift. A spring tire changeover is the moment when a tech has the best view of your wheels, your tires, and any wear patterns that developed over winter. Catching alignment problems at that moment costs nothing extra — you are already there.

The financial answer: alignment issues wear tires. If you put a fresh set of all-seasons or summers on a car with bad alignment, you are burning through tread unevenly from kilometre one. Depending on how far out of spec you are, misalignment can shorten the life of a tire edge by a year or two. Getting alignment sorted before you put real spring and summer mileage on new tires is just math.

The timing answer: you want to act after Calgary's main pothole damage is done (late March or early April), but before mountain trips and long summer drives. Get your alignment checked in April and you have a full season on properly set-up wheels. Wait until August and you have already logged thousands of kilometres on a misaligned car.

How to work an alignment check into your spring routine

The easiest approach: book your tire changeover at Prince Tires first. When your winters come off, we can tell you whether the wear pattern is worth flagging to a mechanic. Then take that information to an auto shop and ask specifically for a four-wheel alignment check. That is a twenty-minute conversation that can save you a tire set.

If you already know there is a problem — you have been driving on a pull all winter — book the alignment before the changeover if you can. Coming in with a properly aligned car means your fresh tires start wearing correctly from the first kilometre.

Either way, getting both done in the same week in April is about as sensible as spring maintenance gets. It is the Calgary driving equivalent of checking your spare before you drive the Icefields Parkway — simple things that prevent expensive problems later.

Frequently asked questions

Does Prince Tires do wheel alignment?

Not directly. Prince Tires focuses on tires and wheels: changeovers, balancing, rotation, flat repair, TPMS service, and wheel sales. For alignment itself, you will need a licensed auto shop with an alignment rack. We are happy to flag what the wear pattern on your outgoing tires suggests before you go.

How do I know if my alignment needs checking after winter?

Try the steering wheel test on a straight, flat stretch: let go briefly and see if the car drifts. Also check your outgoing winter tires for edge wear concentrated on one side. A visible pull to one side or a crooked steering wheel at speed are the clearest signs. When in doubt, ask the tech at your spring changeover — the tires coming off are usually diagnostic on their own.

Why is spring better than fall for alignment in Calgary?

Spring catches the damage winter actually caused. Pothole season runs February through April in Calgary, and that is when most alignment gets knocked out of spec. Checking in spring means you know the full scope of winter damage before you put summer kilometres on fresh tires. Fall alignment checks are reasonable too, but they catch less because the summer road season is relatively gentle on wheels.

Can I drive with bad alignment for a while?

You can, but every kilometre is burning tread unevenly. Misalignment accelerates edge wear significantly — a serious case can shorten the life of a tire edge by years, not months. Steering and suspension components also take more stress than they should. The longer you leave it, the more expensive the eventual fix becomes between tires and parts.

Should I get alignment done before or after new tires at Prince Tires?

Ideally before. Get the alignment checked first so your fresh tires start correctly from kilometre zero. If that is not logistically possible, get the tires mounted and balanced at Prince Tires first, then book alignment immediately after. Do not wait a full season — you will just wear through the tread unevenly in the meantime.
